洗.meaning: <part>water drops</part> splash onto a pair of muddy <part>legs</part> caked in <part>soil</part>. A <part>slash</part> of soap, a good scrub, and the legs come out pink and clean. Time to <kanji>wash</kanji>.
洗.on: A sentry at the door won't let anyone in until they wash. The first part of sentry, 'sen': <reading>せん</reading>.
洗.kun: Under the warm water, the clean legs cheer 'Ah! Rah! Ooh!' Ah-rah-oo: <reading>あらう</reading>. <ja>洗う</ja> is to wash.

使.meaning: A <part>leaning person</part> grabs a megaphone: a <part>one</part>-plank handle, a <part>mouth</part> to shout through and a <part>slash</part> of strap. Megaphone, spoon, shoe: whatever is in reach, they put it to <kanji>use</kanji>.
使.on: They even use a knight's shield as a tray for tea and biscuits. The start of shield, 'shee': <reading>し</reading>.
使.kun: 'Two cars? Ooh!' They'll use both. Say 'two' with a hiss, then 'kah-oo': tsu-kah-oo, <reading>つかう</reading>. <ja>使う</ja> is to use.

五.meaning: A number 5 got jammed between a ceiling bar and a floor bar and bent in the middle where it was squashed. It's crooked now, but count it anyway: it's still a <kanji>five</kanji>.
五.on: A gorilla holds up one hand, all fingers out, to show you how many bananas it wants. Its short first syllable, 'go': <reading>ご</reading>.
五.kun: 'It's five!' the gorilla insists. Say 'it's', short and quick: eet-su, <reading>いつつ</reading>. <ja>五つ</ja> is five things.

弓.meaning: One stroke bends back and forth three times, like a bow pulled tight with a curl at each tip. Notch an arrow, draw back the string, and let fly: it's a <kanji>bow</kanji>.
弓.on: Out of arrows, the archer fires a pool cue from the bow instead. Cue is the held 'kyoo': <reading>きゅう</reading>.
弓.kun: The archer points at you, then at herself: 'You, me!' Yoo-mee, both short: <reading>ゆみ</reading>, a bow.

引.meaning: Next to the <part>bow</part> stands a <part>pole</part>: the arrow, ready to go. You hook it on the string and <kanji>pull</kanji> it back as far as it will stretch, arms shaking.
引.on: The arrow's tip was dipped in a pot of ink, and it leaves a black line on your cheek. Ink, drop the k, 'in': <reading>いん</reading>.
引.kun: You pull so hard on the string that you get the hiccups: 'Hic!' Hee-koo: <reading>ひく</reading>. <ja>引く</ja> is to pull.

値.meaning: A <part>leaning person</part> runs a market stall: a <part>ten</part> sign on top, an <part>eye</part> peering out below, a <part>pole</part> and a <part>one</part>-plank counter. The eye looks each shopper up and down, and everyone gets a different <kanji>price</kanji>.
値.on: A cheetah snatches the price tag and sprints off with it. The first part of cheetah, 'chee': <reading>ち</reading>.
値.kun: The price tag ends up hanging on the stall keeper's necktie. 'Ah! Tie!' Ah-tie: <reading>あたい</reading>, the price.

身.meaning: A body seen from the side: a head on top, ribs as lines across the middle, one leg stepping out at the bottom and an arm swinging. Nobody in particular, just a body walking by: <kanji>somebody</kanji>.
身.on: Somebody walking by isn't looking and kicks you right in the shin. Shin is 'shin': <reading>しん</reading>.
身.kun: A meerkat stands up straight on its hind legs, looking like somebody. The first part of meerkat, 'mee': <reading>み</reading>.

薬.meaning: Under a cap of <part>grass</part>, a <part>white</part> pill sits between two <part>loop</part> ribbons, all balanced on top of a little <part>tree</part>. The herbalist picks the pill off the tree like a ripe fruit and hands it to you: <kanji>medicine</kanji>.
薬.on: A yapping puppy refuses its medicine and yaps at the spoon. Yap, close to 'yaku': <reading>やく</reading>.
薬.kun: The cuckoo swallows its pill and lets out a screech. Its short 'ku', then 'suri' squeezed into the 'sree' of screech: ku-sree, <reading>くすり</reading>.

高.meaning: A tower: a <part>lid</part> of a roof, a <part>mouth</part> window, then a big <part>frame</part> of a ground floor with another mouth for a door. Stack floors like that, one on another, and it gets <kanji>tall</kanji>.
高.on: On the very top sits a giant ice cream cone sign you can see from anywhere. Cone without the n, a held 'koh': <reading>こう</reading>.
高.kun: You climb so high you tack a flag to the top. 'Tack-a': tah-kah, <reading>たかい</reading>. <ja>高い</ja> is tall or expensive.

価.meaning: A <part>leaning person</part> lugs home a crate from the <part>west</part>, where it was dirt cheap. Back home they open it and everyone gasps: it's worth a fortune here. Same crate, a new <kanji>value</kanji>.
価.on: The crate turns out to be full of cabbages, and they sell for gold. The short start of cabbage, 'ka': <reading>か</reading>.
価.kun: Like a price tag, the crate's value hangs on a necktie: 'Ah! Tie!' Ah-tie: <reading>あたい</reading>, value.

便.meaning: A <part>leaning person</part> builds a tiny shop: a <part>one</part>-plank roof, <part>rice field</part> shelves lit by a <part>sun</part> lamp, a <part>pole</part> in the middle and a <part>slash</part> of a door. Glue, snacks, batteries, a step from home: pure <kanji>convenience</kanji>.
便.on: There's even a rubbish bin right by the door, so you don't have to walk far. Bin is 'bin': <reading>びん</reading>.
便.kun: The shop has one pot of yogurt left. 'Tah-dah!' says the clerk. Tah, then the short 'yo' of yogurt: <reading>たより</reading>.

両.meaning: Inside a <part>frame</part> under a <part>one</part>-plank top, a <part>pole</part> splits a tiny <part>mountain</part> into two peaks, left and right. You can't climb just one. You have to conquer <kanji>both</kanji>.
両.on: A dancer in a leotard leaps from one peak to the other. Say 'lee-oh' fast as one held sound, 'ryoh': <reading>りょう</reading>.
両.kun: The dancer wants everyone to know: 'Tell both peaks!' Tell, then a soft 'roo': teh-roo, <reading>てる</reading>.

弁.meaning: An <part>elbow</part> juts up over <part>two hands</part> gripping a pipe. The hands twist, the elbow strains, and with a squeak it finally turns. Hiss: the water stops. It was a stuck <kanji>valve</kanji>.
弁.on: When it's done, the valve handle is bent from all that twisting. Bent, drop the t, 'ben': <reading>べん</reading>.
弁.kun: The plumber shouts to his mum: 'Wacky pipes, Ma!' Wah-kee-mah: <reading>わきまえる</reading>. <ja>弁える</ja> is to know what's proper.

辛.meaning: A pepper <part>stand</part> sells chilies under a sign: <part>ten</part> out of ten heat. Bite one and you leap up as if you'd stood on a nail. Hot, hot, <kanji>spicy</kanji>!
辛.on: Leaping around, you kick the chili stand and bang your shin on it. Shin is 'shin': <reading>しん</reading>.
辛.kun: Your mouth is on fire, so you grab a cabbage to cool it, then lasso a second one. Ka from cabbage, ra from lasso (a light r): <reading>からい</reading>. <ja>辛い</ja> is spicy.

親.meaning: Someone balances on a <part>stand</part> at the top of a <part>tree</part>: a <part>lid</part> of a hat, <part>horns</part> of messy hair, a face red as a <part>chili</part>. They watch the playground through <part>binoculars</part>, never losing sight of one kid. That's a <kanji>parent</kanji>.
親.on: Through the binoculars they see their kid kick another kid's shin. Shin is 'shin': <reading>しん</reading>.
親.kun: 'Oh, yah, I saw that,' the parent calls down from the top of the tree. Oh-yah: <reading>おや</reading>, a parent.

苦.meaning: A <part>mouth</part> is made to chew <part>ten</part> bitter handfuls of <part>grass</part>, one after another. It gags on the third. By the tenth it is pure <kanji>suffering</kanji>.
苦.on: A cuckoo pops out of its clock to count each handful. The short first syllable of cuckoo, 'ku': <reading>く</reading>.
苦.kun: 'Cruel!' the mouth cries between handfuls. The start of cruel, 'koo-roo': <reading>くるしい</reading>. <ja>苦しい</ja> is painful.

落.meaning: <part>grass</part> and <part>water drops</part> drip from the roof onto a <part>slow walker</part> shuffling below, <part>mouth</part> open, staring at the sky. The step is wet, his foot slides, and down he goes: a <kanji>fall</kanji>.
落.on: A raccoon falls off the roof right after him and lands on his chest. The first part of raccoon, 'rak': <reading>らく</reading>.
落.kun: Flat on his back with a raccoon on top, he moans 'Oh… cheese.' Oh-chee: <reading>おちる</reading>. <ja>落ちる</ja> is to fall.

言.meaning: A little box at the bottom, and above it three lines and a dot rising like steam off a cup. That box is a mouth, and the lines are words floating out of it. Open up, and that's what you <kanji>say</kanji>.
言.on: 'Say it again!' shouts the crowd. Keep the end of 'again' with a hard g, 'gen': <reading>げん</reading>.
言.kun: You taste the cold soup and say just one thing: 'Eee-ooh!' Ee-oo: <reading>いう</reading>. <ja>言う</ja> is to say.

計.meaning: <part>speech</part> beside a <part>ten</part>: a general whispers ten short speeches to ten soldiers, one each. No soldier hears the others, so none of them knows the whole <kanji>plot</kanji>.
計.on: Step one of the plot: hide a file inside a birthday cake. Cake, drop the k at the end, 'kay': <reading>けい</reading>.
計.kun: Step two: hack the castle clock. Hack, then 'ah': hah-kah, <reading>はかる</reading>. <ja>計る</ja> is to measure or plan.

長.meaning: Hair streams down from the top in three lines, a stroke for a walking stick, and a robe sweeps the ground. An old wizard whose hair, beard and robe have grown for a hundred years. Everything about him is <kanji>long</kanji>.
長.on: He ties back all that long hair with a tight choker. Choker, a held 'choh': <reading>ちょう</reading>.
長.kun: His hair is so long that everyone nags him to cut it. Nag, then 'ah': nah-gah, <reading>ながい</reading>. <ja>長い</ja> is long.

夫.meaning: A <part>large</part> figure stands with arms wide, but this <part>person</part> has <part>two</part> crossbars instead of one: the top bar is a <part>lid</part> of a top hat, pinned on for the wedding. He's ready to say 'I do': the <kanji>husband</kanji>.
夫.on: His wedding top hat is covered in fuzz from the back of the cupboard. A short, soft 'fu': <reading>ふ</reading>.
夫.kun: At the wedding, the husband backs into a totem pole: 'Oh—!' a sharp stop, then the short 'to' of totem. Ot-to: <reading>おっと</reading>, a husband.

歯.meaning: A kid bites straight into a <part>bucket</part> of raw <part>rice</part>. Crack! Up goes a <part>stop</part> sign, too late. Lying in the rice is something small and white that isn't a grain at all. It's a <kanji>tooth</kanji>.
歯.on: You brush your teeth using a knight's shield as a mirror. The start of shield, 'shee': <reading>し</reading>.
歯.kun: 'Ha!' you grin into the shiny shield, flashing every clean tooth. Ha: <reading>は</reading>, a tooth.

札.meaning: A <part>zigzag</part> of string hangs from a <part>tree</part> branch, with a paper label on the end: 'Apples, two coins.' Every tree in the orchard wears one. It's a price <kanji>tag</kanji>.
札.on: A satellite in orbit zooms in and reads every tag from space. The first part of satellite, 'sat': <reading>さつ</reading>.
札.kun: The biggest tag just says 'Food!' with an arrow. 'Food, ah!' Foo-dah: <reading>ふだ</reading>, a tag.

戻.meaning: Through a <part>door</part>, a <part>one</part>-plank top over a <part>flag</part>, stomps a <part>large</part> dog. You shoo it out. It trots straight back in. Every time, it will <kanji>revert</kanji> to the same spot on the rug.
戻.on: Behind the dog, a stingray glides back in through the door too, flapping. Ray is 'ray': <reading>れい</reading>.
戻.kun: The dog comes back with a toy dolphin in its mouth and mumbles 'Mo…' through it. 'Mo', then the short 'do' of dolphin: mo-do, <reading>もどす</reading>. <ja>戻す</ja> is to put back.

冷.meaning: Under an <part>umbrella</part>, a clerk sits at a <part>one</part>-plank desk with a <part>stamp</part>, while <part>ice</part> chips rain down beside them. Stamp, stamp: the queue shivers. It's <kanji>cool</kanji> in here.
冷.on: A stingray slides by under the ice, cold and silent, and the clerk stamps it too. Ray is 'ray': <reading>れい</reading>.
冷.kun: Two frozen hands: say 'two' with a hiss, then the 'me' of 'met'. Tsu-meh: <reading>つめたい</reading>. <ja>冷たい</ja> is cold.

酒.meaning: <part>water drops</part> trickle into a <part>jug</part> of rice and sit for weeks in a dark shed. When the lid comes off, the drops have turned into something much stronger: <kanji>sake</kanji>, rice wine.
酒.on: The brewer tips in a pile of sugar cubes to help it along. The short first sound of sugar, 'shu': <reading>しゅ</reading>.
酒.kun: The brewer straps the jug to a saddle and, at camp, warms it in a kettle. The 'sa' of saddle and the 'ke' of kettle: sa-ke, <reading>さけ</reading>.

皿.meaning: Seen from the side: a flat base, and on top a shallow tray split into sections by little walls, like a lunch tray. Pile food in each section: it's a <kanji>dish</kanji>.
皿.on: The dish is piled with shrimp, fresh from the boats in the bay. Bay is 'bay': <reading>べい</reading>.
皿.kun: Leave it out and the dish dries out like the Sahara. Drop the middle 'ha': sah-rah, <reading>さら</reading>.

血.meaning: A <part>dish</part> sits on the table with one drop falling into it from above. Plink. A single red drop, then another, then another. Someone's finger is cut: it's <kanji>blood</kanji>.
血.on: At a picnic, a bat swoops down on your hotdog. It doesn't want blood after all: it licks off the ketchup and flies away. The first part of ketchup, 'ketch': <reading>けつ</reading>.
血.kun: A cheetah scratches your arm, and this time it's real. The first part of cheetah, 'chee': <reading>ち</reading>.

町.meaning: Next to a <part>rice field</part>, a <part>crowbar</part> hangs from a <part>one</part>-plank sign: someone has opened a hardware shop. Then come a baker, a school, a post office. The field has grown into a <kanji>town</kanji>.
町.on: The fanciest shop in town sells nothing but chokers. Choker, a held 'choh': <reading>ちょう</reading>.
町.kun: The town's very first shop sold only matches. 'Match', then 'ee': mah-chee, <reading>まち</reading>, a town.

又.meaning: Two strokes cross like a hand reaching out, palm down, to grab the last cookie. Caught? It grabs another. And another. Will it stop now, <kanji>or again</kanji>?
又.on: A unicorn trots in and eats all the cookies again. The first part of unicorn, a held 'yoo': <reading>ゆう</reading>.
又.kun: 'Ma! Ta-da!' the kid calls, holding up yet another cookie. Mah-tah: <reading>また</reading>, again and again.
